facts.rationale: Corrects the blanket previous-family exclusion and extra-zero claim while preserving the exact equality override. Describes source data, not compiled section layout.
facts.value: The source aggregate partitions fourteen attacks into five operative ranges: indices 0–2, 3–6, 7–9, 10–11 and 12–13. Selection indexes a five-byte row using prior category x224C. Row zero is [1,2,3,4,0], permitting category zero to repeat; rows one through four exclude their own category and contain zero twice. The sixth row and range pair are zero-filled. Exact equality of x2254 and attribute x24 bypasses the matrix and forces category 2. Selecting category 2 resets x2254; other selections increment it. A random index within the chosen range resolves through the index and motion-state arrays.

facts.rationale: Distinguishes syntactic alternatives from reachable data flow and preserves the unchanged depth component.
facts.value: Obtains the Master Hand Fighter and special attributes, sets x2258 to Wait1_0 and motion_id to Entry, then copies x30_pos2.x/y into cur_pos without assigning cur_pos.z. The Entry marker forces the subsequent position branch to copy the complete cur_pos into x2240_pos. The preset Wait1_0 marker makes the embedded Wait1_2 frame-preservation branch unreachable, so Fighter_ChangeMotionState receives frame zero, speed one and blend zero for Wait1_0. The helper finally writes Wait1_0 to x2258 again.

facts.rationale: Corrects the own-selection read claim and documents cross-file by-value destination storage and deferred callback execution.
facts.value: Reads player-slot type, current motion, countdown x223C, CPU level, timing input x2238, prior category x224C, counter x2254, suppression flag x221D_b4, attributes, selection tables, stage geometry and random samples. Its continuation helpers also read animation frame, private wait marker and position anchor. On timer expiry it reloads x223C; ordinary selection writes x224C and x2250 and updates x2254 before suppression changes only the local dispatch value. The callback does not directly read its own x2250. Combination handling separately queries Crazy Hand's current motion and, through ftBossLib_8015C4C4, Crazy Hand's stored x2250. Position-based dispatch passes a stack destination and callback to ftMh_MS_389_80150DC4, which copies the destination into fighter state and stores the callback for later arrival processing. Other branches call direct setup routines; combination Slam only fills the unused local vector.

evidence.why: Complete held-button ladder and combination exceptions.
Accessor reads stored x2250 and returns zero if Crazy Hand is absent.

facts.rationale: Preserves exact priority and exceptional no-dispatch paths without converting cross-character selection tokens into unverified public move names.
facts.value: Evaluates held buttons from HSD_PadMasterStatus[2] in one else-if ladder, in this priority: L+Up/Right/Down, R+Up/Right/Down/Left, A+Up/Right/Down, B+Up/Right, Z+Up/Right, Y+Up. These branches select the source-commented stage-wide slap/sweep/walk, drill/punch/ground slap/poke, jet/ram/crush, lasers/gun, grab variants and combination handling, respectively. Z+Up writes ftMh_MS_Throw and Z+Right writes ftMh_MS_Slam to x2250 before calling the shared grab approach. Y+Up reads Crazy Hand's stored selection, not its current motion: Squeezing1, Squeeze and Throw supply x124_pos, x12C_pos and x134_pos with callbacks ftMh_MS_380_80155194, ftMh_MS_382_801552F8 and ftMh_MS_383_80155484. The Slam case only constructs a local position from x13C_pos and dispatches nothing. Unmatched selections or chords make no local transition. At most one chord branch executes per call; this is not an edge-triggered input test.
